extraction.name: SWE-rebench
extraction.description: SWE-rebench is a public dataset comprising over 21,000 interactive Python-based software engineering tasks extracted from diverse GitHub repositories. It is designed for reinforcement learning of SWE agents at scale and includes a continuously updated, contamination-free benchmark for agentic software engineering evaluation. Each task instance includes a GitHub issue description, solution patch, test patch, installation configuration, and LLM-assessed quality scores.
extraction.license: Permissive open-source licenses including MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-4-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, BSD-2-Clause, ISC, CC0-1.0, ZPL-2.1, and other manually verified permissive licenses
extraction.creator: Nebius (Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev, Maksim Nekrashevich, Anton Shevtsov, Simon Karasik, Andrei Andriushchenko, Maria Trofimova, Daria Litvintseva, Boris Yangel)
extraction.citeAs: Badertdinov et al. SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents. 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025) Track on Datasets and Benchmarks. arXiv:2505.20411v2 [cs.SE] 4 Nov 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is collected via a fully automated, scalable pipeline that continuously extracts real-world interactive software engineering tasks from diverse GitHub repositories. The pipeline comprises four stages: preliminary task collection (downloading and filtering pull requests linked to issues from GitHub Archive and GitHub), automated installation instruction configuration (LLM-driven generation of environment setup recipes), execution-based installation verification (running tests in containers to confirm task solvability), and automated instance quality assessment (fine-tuned LLM predicting issue clarity, task complexity, and test patch correctness). Approximately 450,000 pull requests from over 30,000 repositories were initially downloaded, filtered down to ~153,400 candidates, and ultimately yielding 21,336 valid annotated task instances from 3,468 distinct GitHub repositories.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The pipeline successfully produces a working installation recipe for at least one task in 31% of all repositories. The automated dependency installation stage has a current success rate of approximately 14% (from ~150K filtered tasks to ~21K valid tasks), representing a significant bottleneck. Failure modes include flaky tests with external API calls or floating-point precision issues, lack of interactivity during installation, and unpinned or obsolete dependencies.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Primary sources are GitHub Archive (public events on GitHub, including issue descriptions, discussions, linked pull requests, and metadata) and GitHub (cloned repositories with full commit histories). Approximately 450,000 pull requests linked to issues created before May 1, 2025, from over 30,000 repositories where Python constitutes over 75% of codebase lines of code and with permissive licenses.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Pull requests linked to issues created before May 1, 2025. The benchmark subset focuses on issues created in 2025 (January and March-April 2025 subsets used for evaluation).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For each selected pull request, the overall patch is divided into two components: a solution patch (changes to non-test files) and a test patch (changes to test files only). Task instances are grouped by project versions inferred from git tag outputs, normalizing versions to major.minor format. The pipeline prioritizes diffing head_commit against base_commit to generate patches, falling back to merge_commit if head_commit is unavailable. Deleted files are filtered out from test directives. Dependency versions are frozen and recorded after successful environment setup using pip freeze and conda env export.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preliminary filtering selects instances where: the issue is from a Python repository with a permissive license, the issue is marked as resolved, the PR is merged into the main branch, the PR is not linked to multiple issues, the issue description is longer than 10 characters, the PR introduces or modifies tests and includes code changes beyond test files, and changes affect 1 to 15 files. Execution-based verification ensures: at least one test from the test patch fails before applying the solution patch, all initially failing tests pass after the solution patch, and initially passing tests continue to pass. Flaky tests (failing in at least one run) are excluded. For the benchmark subset, additional filters include: clean test execution logs (no AttributeError or ImportError), solution patch modifying no more than 3 files, solution patch containing no more than 500 words, problem statement between 16 and 1000 words in English, issue created in 2025, LLM-assessed difficulty label less than 3, and no more than 50 fail-to-pass tests.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Automated quality assessment is performed by fine-tuning a Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct model on human annotations from SWE-bench Verified (over 3,800 examples) to predict three binary quality labels: Issue Clarity (whether the GitHub issue description is sufficiently detailed), Task Complexity (estimated effort to resolve the issue), and Test Patch Correctness (whether tests accurately verify the intended fix). Each task instance is assessed for each quality characteristic separately using a 75/25 training/validation split (413 validation examples). LLM-generated labels are provided as metadata with each task instance.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Fine-tuned Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct model; human annotations sourced from SWE-bench Verified
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For Task Complexity, the fine-tuned model achieved 81% accuracy and weighted F1-score of 0.82 (vs. 68% accuracy for baseline Qwen-72B-Instruct). For Test Patch Correctness, the model achieved 67% accuracy (weighted F1: 0.65). For Issue Clarity, it achieved 79% accuracy (weighted F1: 0.76). Detailed precision and recall per class are reported. The automated assessment is acknowledged as imperfect and cannot fully replicate nuanced human judgment.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: SWE-rebench uses an automated pipeline for continuous supply of fresh tasks. The leaderboard is continuously updated with new tasks and model evaluations. The dataset is publicly available on Hugging Face Datasets. The team tracks creation dates of issues and pull requests against model release dates to explicitly mark potentially contaminated evaluations. Future work includes expanding data coverage, improving task filtering, supporting new programming languages, and maintaining evaluation on fresh tasks.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: SWE-rebench may accelerate the development of increasingly autonomous AI systems in software engineering. This progress brings potential risks, such as overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities. The authors believe that fostering openness, decontaminated evaluations, and rigorous benchmarking practices helps mitigate these concerns and contributes to responsible advancement of the field.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The initial release is limited exclusively to Python repositories, restricting applicability to other language ecosystems. The dataset is sourced only from repositories with permissive licenses. The automated quality assessment, while scalable, contains errors and may decrease dataset quality compared to manual curation. The LLM-based approach to generating installation instructions was validated on a limited set of 18 repositories and may not capture every project's subtleties.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The fully automated pipeline may result in some tasks being imperfectly described or unsolvable solely from the issue, leading to lower absolute success rates compared to manually curated benchmarks. The dataset is limited exclusively to Python, restricting immediate applicability to other language ecosystems. The automated task quality assessment cannot fully replicate nuanced human judgment. The pipeline relies on heuristics and LLM-driven interpretations. Flaky tests, unpinned dependencies, and projects requiring interactive installation are common failure modes.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training (particularly reinforcement learning of SWE agents at scale), Testing, and Evaluation of LLM-based software engineering agents. The dataset is suitable for benchmarking agents in diverse executable environments. LLM-generated quality scores facilitate task difficulty control for more nuanced task selection for model training or evaluation needs. The benchmark subset (294 tasks from 169 repositories) is used for standardized, decontaminated evaluation via a public leaderboard.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 (Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, Test Patch Correctness)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (for generating installation recipes and quality assessment labels); fine-tuned Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct (for predicting Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, and Test Patch Correctness); TractoAI (distributed storage and computing platform for parallel processing)
